subject: Integrate "a limit is missing" error in gdistsamp

messages.author: d4a835914e61fc5b
messages.subject: Integrate "a limit is missing" error in gdistsamp
parts:
Hello, Unmarked Group!

 

I am running gdistsamp on a dataset including 4 years of point count data where each point was visited up to 4 times (only once/year).  Andy mentioned that gdistsamp should work with yearly visits (https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!searchin/unmarked/royle$20gdistsamp$20kendrick/unmarked/UDYbyfKUup0/2phiL_k3zT0J).


I created my unmarked frame using this code:

umf<-with(alldata2,{

  unmarkedFrameGDS(y=cbind(Y2003_D1,Y2003_D2,Y2003_D3,Y2004_D1,Y2004_D2,Y2004_D3,Y2005_D1,Y2005_D2,Y2005_D3,Y2006_D1,Y2006_D2,Y2006_D3),

                   siteCovs=data.frame(lowrip,mesic,cc,for1k,for5k,for10k,nonfor,water,edge,ESpatch,ESedge,patch4,patch8,

                                       everg,grasture,age,HSIval),

                   yearlySiteCovs=data.frame(mins03,mins04,mins05,mins06,day03,day04,day05,day06),

                   dist.breaks=c(25,50,100),

                   survey="point",

                   unitsIn="m",

                   numPrimary=4). 

When I try to run a null model with a Poisson distribution

(HZ_Null_P<-gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha", mixture="P", output="density", data=umf)), I receive the following error:

Error in integrate(grhaz, db[j], db[j + 1], shape = shape[i, t], scale = scale,  :

  a limit is missing


I found Erik’s post re: a limit is missing (https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!searchin/unmarked/erik$20a$20limit$20is$20missing/unmarked/1fRKMlHakqY/ugkyfiaqfvgJ), and I even tried changing numPrimary to no avail, and it makes sense that my numPrimary=4, because there were 4 occasions/years for a point to be sampled). Also, points not visited all 4 years were padded with NAs, as suggested (https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!searchin/unmarked/pad$20NA/unmarked/9PzpkqoSJuw/3Be-5XXfETkJ).

 

Any help would be much appreciated.  Below is a summary(umf) .

 

Thanks so much,

Sarah

Hi Sarah,

The first "dist.break" should be 0. unmarked isn't set up to handle left-truncation. 

Richard
